headline: US Navy 3D prints combat-ready drones and 1,000+ parts aboard aircraft carrier
summary: During a two-week transit, a containerized factory aboard the USS Essex 3D printed a dozen flight-ready drones and over 1,000 parts, including vital spares, despite rough seas and 12-foot waves.
details: During a two-week transit to RIMPAC 2026, the USS Essex hosted Firestorm Labs' xCell containerized factory. This platform successfully 3D printed a dozen flight-ready Squall FPV drones and over 1,000 other parts, including critical spares for Apache helicopters. Production continued uninterrupted despite rough seas and waves up to 12 feet.

This marked the first maritime deployment of the xCell expeditionary manufacturing platform. Firestorm Labs stated this milestone proved "expeditionary manufacturing works in real conditions," enabling on-demand production at sea.

The xCell production line fits into two expandable 20-foot ISO containers, or a single 40-foot equivalent. It houses industrial HP Multi Jet Fusion polymer printers alongside semi-automated assembly stations, making it a compact and robust solution.

The Squall FPV drones, a key Firestorm Labs product, boast a range of up to 20 miles, a flight time of 42 minutes, and a top speed of 80 mph, capable of carrying a 5.5-pound payload. These drones were later used as adversary aircraft in a counter-UAS exercise upon arrival at RIMPAC.

Beyond drones, essential parts like Apache helicopter rotor droop-stops were printed, preventing potential $500,000 rotor damage. Custom vacuum-hose couplings for life preserver testing and various crew-requested gadgets were also produced.

Firestorm Labs highlighted the logistical advantages, noting that "Every part xCell printed on deck is one that doesn't need to be flown or shipped across contested waters." This significantly cuts fuel, aircraft hours, and personnel needed, allowing repairs to happen in hours instead of weeks.

headline_marked: AMD Ryzen 7 7700X3D vs [[7800X3D faceoff]]: seeing double with Zen 4 X3D
headline: AMD Ryzen 7 7700X3D vs 7800X3D faceoff: seeing double with Zen 4 X3D
summary: AMD's new Ryzen 7 7700X3D offers 3D V-Cache at a lower price point, but how does it stack up against its popular sibling, the 7800X3D?
details: AMD recently expanded its X3D lineup with the Ryzen 7 7700X3D, a new entry that slots in below the Ryzen 7 7800X3D as a more affordable way to get 3D V-Cache on the AM5 platform. Launched on July 16 at $329, the 7700X3D is essentially built from the same silicon as the 7800X3D, just with lower clocks and a price tag that undercuts it by $120 at launch.

The Ryzen 7 7800X3D, launched in April 2023 at $449 (now $360), quickly became one of the most recommended gaming CPUs on the market and has held that reputation. AMD has kept it in the lineup even as newer X3D chips took the place at the top of the best CPU for gaming charts.

With the 7700X3D now available, AM5 builders finally have a cheaper way into the X3D club without stepping down to the six-core Ryzen 5 7600X3D. The obvious question is how much performance actually gets left on the table by going with the cheaper option, and whether the 7800X3D's higher clocks are worth the extra money.

The Ryzen 7 7700X3D features 8 cores and 16 threads, with a base clock of 4.0 GHz and a boost clock of 4.5 GHz. This boost clock is 500 MHz lower than the 7800X3D. AMD has essentially taken 7800X3D silicon that couldn't hit the higher clocks and repackaged it as a cheaper SKU. It carries the full 96MB of 3D V-Cache-enabled L3, for a total cache pool of 104MB.

The Ryzen 7 7800X3D also has 8 cores and 16 threads, built on the same Zen 4 architecture and TSMC's N5 node. It separates itself with a 4.2 GHz base clock and a considerably higher 5.0 GHz boost clock. It also carries the same 96MB of L3 cache and 104MB total cache figure.

Neither CPU officially supports traditional multiplier overclocking. However, AMD has gradually opened up more headroom for Curve Optimizer and PBO tuning on its X3D lineup since the 7800X3D's launch. This comparison will delve into that in more detail.

Both CPUs use the AM5 socket, support DDR5 memory exclusively (up to 128 GB), and feature PCIe 5.0 connectivity. They also share the same 120W TDP and integrated graphics in the form of AMD Radeon Graphics with 2 CUs running at 2,200 MHz.

Zooming out, it's clear these two CPUs are much closer than a typical faceoff matchup. The only meaningful difference on paper is the 500 MHz deficit on the 7700X3D's boost clock, and any price gap that comes with it. The 7800X3D still wins on paper thanks to its higher boost clock, but barely.
